profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting for the internal service 'Advaita', which flags likely duplicate bug reports inside the company's Jira-based bug tracker. Over the last two weeks, triagers have complained that Advaita is surfacing obviously unrelated duplicates for freshly filed bugs in the Payments and Identity products, while also missing some near-identical reports that used to be caught. The meeting happens after a small model refresh and a bug-tracker schema update that added a new component taxonomy. The agenda is to diagnose why duplicate suggestions degraded, determine whether the problem is in feature generation, model serving, or ticket ingestion, and agree on a same-day mitigation plus a follow-up fix. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting plan, an owner for the immediate rollback/patch, and agreement on what 'stabilized' behavior means for today's incident response.

members.name: Nisha Rao
members.expertise: NLP systems, feature pipelines, model evaluation, offline/online consistency
members.background: Nisha built the current Advaita duplicate-classification model six months ago and recently refreshed the training set with newer Jira tickets; she mostly works from offline experiments and model-service logs rather than day-to-day triage operations.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid a full rollback because she believes the refreshed model is broadly better and worries that if the issue is blamed on the model, the team will pause the roadmap for semantic matching improvements; she suspects a pipeline mismatch but wants to contain the incident quickly.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'duplicate suggestions got worse,' they mainly mean the model's ranking quality at top-5 on the shadow evaluation slice she monitors.
The 'new component taxonomy' is functionally equivalent to the old component field for feature extraction because unmapped values should safely fall back to 'unknown.'
If they 'reindex recent bugs,' that means replaying the last 14 days of ticket text through the feature-generation job, not rebuilding historical candidate embeddings.
A 'fix for today' can be a mitigation that restores previous score distribution even if triagers still see some noisy results in low-volume projects.

members.name: Owen Patel
members.expertise: Jira integrations, ingestion pipelines, search indexing, operational support for triage workflows
members.background: Owen owns the connector that syncs bug reports from Jira into Advaita's candidate store and also handles the schema migration for product/component metadata; he works closely with human triagers and sees issue quality through support tickets and UI behavior.
members.private_state: He wants to protect the recent Jira schema rollout from being seen as the cause and is focused on reducing triager pain today, even if the underlying quality metrics are not fully restored; he suspects the model team underestimates how much metadata drift affects user trust.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'duplicate suggestions,' they mean the three items shown to triagers in the Jira sidebar, after search candidate generation and UI filtering, not the model's raw top-5 ranking.
The 'component field' now refers to the normalized taxonomy node stored after migration, not the legacy free-text component string that older bugs still contain.
If they 'reindex recent bugs,' that means refreshing the search/index layer for newly migrated tickets so the sidebar candidate pool is correct, not rerunning feature extraction.
A bug is 'fixed' for today's incident once triagers stop filing complaints on newly created Payments and Identity tickets, even if historical matching quality remains uneven.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly discuss whether 'duplicate suggestions' have gotten worse.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the classifier's ranked duplicate predictions measured at top-5 before downstream filtering.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the three duplicate cards that triagers actually see in the Jira sidebar after candidate retrieval, UI filtering, and thresholding.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this system the same phrase is routinely used for both the model output and the user-visible sidebar results, and both are usually correlated, so each assumes the other is using the standard shorthand.

misalignment_points.topic: Which component field is in play
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to 'the component feature' and 'component values' as if they are talking about the same field.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the legacy component text tokenized from bug headline/description metadata, which her training pipeline still joins from the pre-migration export.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the newly normalized taxonomy component ID and display label produced by the Jira schema migration.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The migration preserved the label 'component' everywhere in dashboards and logs, and both legacy text and normalized taxonomy values coexist for many bugs, making the reference feel unambiguous in conversation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that they should 'reindex recent bugs today.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means rerunning feature extraction and candidate-vector generation for the last 14 days of ingested tickets used by the duplicate model.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means rebuilding the search documents and sidebar candidate pool for newly migrated Jira issues in the online index.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In past incidents 'reindex' has loosely referred to any bulk refresh of bug data, and each person normally executes only their own subsystem's version without spelling out the implementation details.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on the need to 'stabilize things for today' and confirm a 'fix' before end of day.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'stabilized' means online score distributions and top-5 duplicate precision return close to last week's baseline on incident slices.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'stabilized' means triagers creating new Payments and Identity bugs stop seeing obviously wrong duplicate cards and support noise drops today.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both criteria often improve together during normal operation, so saying 'stable' or 'fixed' usually feels sufficient; under incident pressure, neither pauses to define the acceptance threshold explicitly.

On the shadow slice I watch, duplicate suggestions are down versus last week on recent tickets, but the weights themselves were barely touched in the refresh. If we can get score distributions back in family today, we can preserve the semantic matching work.

turns.utterance: That's possible. One thing I do know is the candidate pool may be skewed right now because only newly migrated issues were refreshed in the online index. We should probably reindex recent bugs today and remove that variable.
